nodes.label: USER-MANUAL PDF Pipeline
nodes.rationale: USER-MANUAL.html is the source; USER-MANUAL.pdf is generated with headless LibreOffice and COMMITTED so the manual can be handed over without a toolchain. The HTML is also written so a browser renders it properly: printing from Chrome gives real rounded corners, shadows and flex layout — everything LibreOffice drops. The committed PDF is the toolchain-free version; the browser is the higher-fidelity one.

nodes.label: LibreOffice HTML Import Limitations
nodes.rationale: Its HTML import is not a browser, and every item was found by rendering the PDF back to images and looking at it. border-radius is silently ignored (generate an image); background-color on an inline span is dropped (put it on a td); background/padding on a div is painted PER LINE so a callout looks like highlighted text (use a single-cell table); border-left on a div likewise gives one stubby bar per line; an empty div with only border-top loses the rule and indents the next block (use hr); margin shorthand on h1-h3 leaves the Heading style indent surviving (use longhand margin-left/padding-left 0); descendant selectors are not resolved (inline styles); tables without cellspacing=0 get white gutters that break a dark header row into segments; flexbox/grid unsupported (tables); cellpadding plus width=100% silently drops the padding; a spacer cell in a SHORT table absorbs leftover width. What works reliably: margin on a p inside a td, and width on a td in an already-full-width table. Always set page-break-inside: avoid on tables or a header row lands on one page and its rows on the next.

nodes.label: assets/managed-by.png Closing Panel
nodes.rationale: A rounded 'Handled and managed by Global Tech Solutions' block generated with ImageMagick rather than styled with CSS, precisely BECAUSE LibreOffice's HTML filter ignores border-radius outright and a styled td prints as a hard rectangle. Uses the retired navy #062B59 and gold #D4AF37, since this asset predates the logo/palette change recorded in CLAUDE.md §5.3.
